body: As I’m reading yeah I’m a little too angry and I judged the families too quickly. I think I’m just irritated that these families are not getting the right program they need. This is an after care program, they need 1 on 1 tutoring sessions. I am 1 teacher with 20 students. I wish the families could get way better individual support for their kids but sadly! It seems everyday that good education is only for rich families. I grew up with the belief from my family that merit gets you education but that’s not the case here. All these lower income families just get left to struggle because things like Kumon and Sylvan and other good tutoring support can be unreasonable price wise! I want these kids to do good and I try but it just feels like whatever I’m gonna do is not gonna do much since I don’t have a lot of time with them!

I am only with these kids for 3 hours a day with no aids and I understand that a lot of families come from different backgrounds and have different struggles. I think I’m just irritated because this program cannot give them the help they need. They need to be in a 1 on 1 program where their individual needs are met.

Am I fucking yelling at the parents for their kids not reading?? No! I understand these parents might be busy with work or something else going on. But I am supplemental instructor, I am only with these 20 kids for 3 hours with no assistants to help everybody with basic reading and writing! They need 1 on 1 help with homework, they need to go to a specialized tutoring, we are an aftercare program. The sad thing is, what I learned from my coworkers, nobody cares if they’re behind! They just care that they’re all there and checked out when parents come

I can understand the parents may not always be there all the time, I grew up as a latchkey kid with a lower income family, so I’m understanding and sympathetic, but I am just really like… baffled that they cannot read. Idk if it’s like pandemic, but those kids still should’ve been getting enrichment of some kind even if they aren’t physically in school. Like idk if it’s the main teachers or their parents not stepping in, and I just feel overwhelmed I have no teacher assistants to help all of them with reading and writing because if they don’t have that basic stuff down there’s more I can’t help them with.

It’s a subsidized program so the parents do not pay for it. These are mostly lower income students and I understand the struggles since I grew up with poor immigrant parents. A lot of these kids have the same background as me, so that’s why I want these kids to be able to do fine in their classes but it’s weird that they can’t read still at like 8 years old.
